note: Curated New England solar / net-metering / REC market / regulatory updates for array operators. Each item is tagged with its state (or "region" for New England-wide, "rec" for REC-market-wide); the page filters to the reader's state. Refreshed by a research agent; verify against the linked source before relying on any figure.

items.title: RI PUC holds Nov 17 evidentiary hearing on Rhode Island Energy's net-metering overhaul (Docket 26-30-EL)
items.summary: The Rhode Island PUC held an evidentiary hearing on Tuesday, November 17, 2026 at 9:30 a.m. in Warwick on Rhode Island Energy's revised net-metering provision (Docket 26-30-EL), which lowers the aggregate ground-mount remote-net-metering cap from 275 MW to 175 MW, extends the qualifying-project deadline to Dec 31, 2032, and adds an optional 25-year 'Fixed Renewable Net Metering Credit' of 19¢/kWh for public, educational, hospital and nonprofit systems. The Office of Energy Resources and Ameresco intervened; the Commission must approve an implementing tariff by Dec 1, 2026.

items.title: Eversource Connecticut rate-case public hearings underway; company pegs the ask near $33/month
items.summary: Eversource's pending PURA distribution rate case (Docket 26-05-10) moved into public comment hearings in November 2026 — sessions were held Nov 9 in New Britain and Nov 16 in New London, with Nov 23 in Danbury and a virtual Dec 9 session to follow. Eversource says the request would raise a typical bill about $33/month; the base distribution ask is roughly 11% starting July 2027, and it also seeks to recover more than $1 billion in 2018–2023 storm costs. AARP Connecticut has urged PURA to reject the increase.

items.title: Vermont PUC holds second Rule 5.100 net-metering workshop (Case 26-1786-RULE)
items.summary: The Vermont Public Utility Commission held a second virtual stakeholder workshop on November 16, 2026 in its rulemaking to update Commission Rule 5.100 (construction and operation of net-metering systems), following the first session on October 2, 2026. The rulemaking, opened by order on September 9, 2026, examines distributed-solar grid impacts and implements Act 38 of 2025, which raised the expedited-registration threshold for ground-mounted systems from 15 kW to 25 kW.

items.title: November 2026 broker quotes put MA Class I RECs near $38/MWh; legacy SREC IIs still above $220
items.summary: As of November 2026, Sol Systems' Massachusetts REC schedule lists Class I certificates at about $38/MWh on a variable brokerage basis (and $29.50/MWh on a two-year fixed annuity), while legacy SREC II certificates are quoted around $221.75 each. The Class I level remains just under the $40/MWh Alternative Compliance Payment ceiling that MA, CT and RI now share.

items.title: Massachusetts DPU opens a net-crediting technical conference (Docket 25-117)
items.summary: The Massachusetts Department of Public Utilities held a technical conference on expanding net crediting (Docket 25-117) on October 27, 2026 — part of its broader work on how solar and net-metering credits are applied to customer bills. It runs parallel to the DPU's Docket 25-200 delivery-rate-design investigation, which is separately weighing whether to reduce the value of net-metering credits.

items.title: Acadia Center: NECEC Quebec hydro lifts New England net imports to their highest since 2022
items.summary: An Acadia Center assessment (published Aug 26, 2026, updated Oct 26, 2026) finds the New England Clean Energy Connect line is adding Quebec hydro imports to regional supply rather than displacing existing Phase II exports: average net imports rose from 798 MW/hour in spring 2025 to 1,625 MW/hour in spring 2026, lifting imports to 13% of regional energy (up from 7%) and putting 2026 net imports on track for their highest level since 2022. The contracts require environmental attributes to be tracked under NEPOOL-GIS, and the hydro is expected to cover most Massachusetts Clean Energy Standard demand, leaving Class I certificates banked for Class I compliance.

items.title: Eversource appeals PURA's storm-cost cut, seeking ~$400M more from Connecticut ratepayers
items.summary: On October 15, 2026 Eversource filed a Connecticut Superior Court appeal challenging PURA's July 2026 final storm-cost decision, which had disallowed roughly $500 million of its ~$1.28 billion request — including about $397 million in retroactive carrying charges. Consumer Counsel Claire Coleman said the Office of Consumer Counsel will keep fighting the request in court and before PURA, calling the appeal costly and meritless.

items.title: Massachusetts DPU technical session (Docket 25-200) weighs trimming net-metering credit value
items.summary: The Massachusetts DPU held a technical session on October 15, 2026 in its delivery-rate-design investigation (Docket 25-200) focused on how the net-metering credit is calculated — which rate components must statutorily remain in the credit, which could be removed, and how any change would affect net-metering customers, developers and ratepayers. No credit reduction has been ordered; the proceeding remains at the technical-conference stage and existing systems are expected to be grandfathered.

items.title: Maine PUC unanimously denies CMP's $69.3M temporary distribution rate increase
items.summary: On October 6, 2026 the Maine Public Utilities Commission voted unanimously to deny Central Maine Power's roughly $69.3 million temporary distribution rate increase (about $7/month for a typical customer), with all three commissioners citing affordability and customer confusion and finding the entire temporary amount 'disputed.' CMP's larger ~$189 million permanent distribution rate case (Docket 2026-00043) remains pending; Chair Phil Bartlett said a decision is most likely in spring 2027 and signaled some increase is probable, though less than CMP requested.

items.title: Massachusetts DOER study finds solar programs return $1.49 per ratepayer dollar
items.summary: On October 1, 2026 the Massachusetts Department of Energy Resources released 'Direct Costs and Benefits of Massachusetts Solar Incentives' (with Synapse and Sustainable Energy Advantage), evaluating SMART and post-2018 net-metering solar from 2018–2025. It found SMART returned $1.49 for every $1 spent — about $11.5 billion in direct lifetime benefits at $7.7 billion cost — and that energy costs, including net metering, make up roughly 79% of total solar compensation cost, the biggest opportunity to improve cost-effectiveness.

items.title: Rooftop solar forces New England to rethink its grid as behind-the-meter PV nears 7,000 MW
items.summary: A Sept 23, 2026 Concord Monitor report notes New England now has roughly 7,000 MW of rooftop and other behind-the-meter solar — capable of producing over five times Seabrook Station's output on a sunny day, and roughly doubling in the last couple of years — after ISO New England logged its 500th 'duck curve' day on Sept 21, 2026 (the 107th of 2026 alone). Analysts say billing and payment mechanisms built for a one-way grid, including net metering, need to adapt to the steep evening ramps.

items.title: Power Advisory: New England basic service rates jump ~14% for 2H 2026, lifting net-metering payouts
items.summary: A Sept 14, 2026 Power Advisory report finds second-half 2026 basic/standard-service supply rates rose about 14% on average across six New England utilities year-over-year — roughly 14% in Massachusetts, 15% in Rhode Island, 25% in New Hampshire and 3% in Connecticut — driven by elevated gas prices, a harsh winter and NECEC underperformance. Because net-metering and community-solar compensation is linked to basic service rates, the analysis notes project owners will see higher payouts, with a further ~12% average increase projected for 1H 2027 (Eversource CT up ~25%).

items.title: Vermont PUC finalizes a 5.5% Green Mountain Power rate increase (Case 26-0096-TF), below the 7.5% requested
items.summary: The Vermont Public Utility Commission's Aug 28, 2026 order approved a 5.5% distribution rate increase for Green Mountain Power's 275,000+ customers — below the 7.5% the utility sought (Case 26-0096-TF) — effective Oct 1, 2026. Regulators approved about $113 million of 'resilience' infrastructure spending, roughly a third of GMP's $341 million request, citing affordability as central to the analysis.

items.title: Power Advisory: New England Class I RECs hold near the $40 ACP into a sixth undersupplied year
items.summary: An August 2026 Power Advisory update reports New England Class I RECs have traded close to the $40 Alternative Compliance Payment through a sixth straight undersupplied year, with forwards (Marex Spectron, as of Aug 13, 2026) still near the cap. Rhode Island has aligned its RES ACP to $40 flat, making the ceiling uniform across MA, CT and RI; separately, NECEC Quebec hydro (delivering since January 2026) is expected to cover nearly all of the Massachusetts Clean Energy Standard requirement in CY2026.

items.title: Acadia Center granted intervenor status in Eversource's Connecticut distribution rate case
items.summary: On August 14, 2026 Acadia Center was granted intervenor status in Eversource's pending PURA rate case, where the utility seeks up to an 18% bill increase (a headline ~$727M once storm costs are included). Acadia is challenging the requested 10.25% return on equity as 'unreasonable and out of step with ROEs nationwide' and is pushing for performance-based ratemaking; new rates would take effect July 1, 2027.

items.title: NH Gov. Ayotte signs SB 538 extending net metering for queued municipal solar
items.summary: SB 538 (Chapter 315, effective Sept 8, 2026) supports municipal solar projects up to 5 MW and guarantees the current net-metering credit for 20 years for cities, towns, school districts and counties whose projects were already in the interconnection queue. It was signed July 10, 2026.
